speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the current status of the shortage of preschool teachers; (b) what efforts are being taken to attract more applicants to join the profession; and (c) how has the shortage affected the operations of childcare centres.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Besides teachers, they include centre supervisors and infant educarers.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The number has increased by over 1,000 in the past two years.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: At the national level, most operators have sufficient manpower to run their centres.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: ECDA has, therefore, implemented various initiatives to attract and retain early childhood educators.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: First, it has expanded intakes for pre-service training courses, such as those at our Polytechnics.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: It is also providing more support to students through training awards and enhanced internships.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Second, ECDA has many more opportunities, through professional conversion programmes for mid-career entrants to join the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Mid-career entrants can work, receive a salary and also attain their professional qualifications at the same time.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: The response on this front has been encouraging.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: Third, ECDA is doing more to retain in-service educators through better skills and career development opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: While we have made some progress with these initiatives, the manpower situation for this sector will remain tight.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
text: ECDA will continue to work closely with employers in the sector to attract and retain early childhood educators.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The second thing I want to ask the Minister is: how many of the childcare centres or early childhood education centres are currently operating below capacity because of manpower shortage?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Which means that, physically, they have the infrastructure, but because they do not have enough teachers, therefore, they cannot bring in the students.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Lastly, I do have many, many childcare centres in my area with a long waiting list.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Unfortunately, due to the physical structure, they cannot take in anymore.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I do have childcare centres whereby there are physical structures but there are not enough teachers at all.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I am just wondering how will the Ministry help to solve this problem.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: There are particular areas where you do have very high demand and where we may not have enough places.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Overall, the numbers may look fine but that is scant consolation to parents because they are looking for places that are nearer their homes.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is where we are continuing to work with the various operators to make sure that the supply of teachers, educarers and so on are coming online.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: As for physical capacity, by and large, that is on track, but in some of the areas where there is high demand, we are also endeavouring to look at where we can set up, physically, new centres as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is something that we are working closely with the sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: By and large, I would say that, at the moment, the plans that we have in place, they do look encouraging but we need to constantly track that.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My question relates to what the Minister commented about efforts to attract and retain people in the industry.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I wonder if the Ministry would consider elevating the awards or the recognition to preschool teachers, similar to that of a Teachers' Day nationwide effort, so that members of the public, parents and everybody will recognise preschool educators as important in the education services and the delivery of the character development of our children.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We will take on board some of these suggestions and we will see how we can implement some of them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: For centres that are currently facing a shortage and possibly cannot even open, cannot even start operating, despite everything already being in place, what will the Ministry be doing, so that it can start operating and help parents who are in desperate need of childcare currently?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We acknowledge that there are some areas where there are shortages simply because of demand in those particular areas.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: So, what we try to do is to work with the centres themselves to see whether we can accelerate the process of setting them up.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: In terms of recruitment and for the parents themselves, we will help them source for the next available centres that are as near as possible to their homes.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have a question pertaining to how we can address a potential shortage in this area, that is, from people with foreign qualifications in this childcare or child education sector.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have come across a couple of Singaporeans, for example, who have studied overseas, they have the relevant qualifications.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am wondering what paths are there for such Singaporeans, or even PRs with these qualifications.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Does ECDA recognise them and, if not, are they obliged to go through an ECDA-certified process before they are allowed to work in the child education industry?

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I fully acknowledge the suggestions put forth by the Member.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: While we recognise that we need to increase the number of teachers to meet demand, I think it is important for us to maintain standards.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I also recognise that there will be those who are educated abroad, trained abroad.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: I think ECDA will be quite happy to review the various considerations in taking them on board.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: Like I have said, the response has been encouraging.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We do encourage individuals who are looking at mid-career switches to consider this as a viable profession.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: With regard to lowering the requirements for educarers, we constantly monitor that.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: We are mindful that it is really about the kind of thresholds that we want to set for the different educators and educarers.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: It is a balance between needing to meet the numbers but, at the same time, making sure that there is a list of basic level requirements to ensure certain standards are met.

speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
text: This is something that we are constantly reviewing, given the different dynamics at play.
